steps.message:
I ran the change-request ladder before touching anything, and this lands on rung 1 — a field name in a response others call — so I'm stopping to confirm before editing.

**The consequence:** `routes/users.js:6` is the only place `userId` is produced, so the edit itself is one word. But it's a breaking change to the `GET /users` response, and `README.md:3-5` records that this response has three consumers — the web app, the iOS app (3.2+), and the nightly partner export — and that "Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint."

Renaming in place means every one of those clients reading `userId` gets `undefined` the moment this deploys. The iOS app is the sharpest edge: shipped versions can't be fixed forward, so 3.2+ installs in the field break until users update. The nightly partner export fails silently — it'll keep running and just emit a null or missing ID column.

"Just the field name" is exactly the scope that's load-bearing here, and the repo's own stated policy is that this goes through a versioned endpoint rather than an in-place rename.

options.description: Follow the README policy: keep /users as-is and add a v2 response shape using user_id. Most work, but matches the documented contract process.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Change userId to user_id at routes/users.js:6 and accept the break. Shipped iOS 3.2+ clients and the nightly partner export will break until they are updated.

steps.message:
Done — one line changed at `routes/users.js:6`. `GET /users` now returns `user_id`, matching `GET /orders`. No `userId` references remain anywhere in the repo, and nothing else was touched.

Two things to flag, since I made the breaking change rather than the compatible one:

- **This ships a breaking response today.** The web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export will read `undefined` for the ID until each is updated. The partner export is the one most likely to fail quietly — worth checking whether it validates its output or just writes a null column.
- **`README.md:3-5` now contradicts the code.** It still states field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. I left it alone because you scoped this to the field name, but it should either be updated or the exception noted, otherwise the next person reads a policy the codebase no longer follows.

There are no tests in this repo, so nothing was run to verify beyond the grep and diff above.
